search_log: Searched “Herman Wouk War and Remembrance excerpt third person narrator point of view”; found and opened the explicit BookRags whole-book POV description.

Searched “War and Remembrance third person omniscient” and related narrator/point-of-view variants; results corroborated third-person narration, though most were summaries or user reviews and were not used.
Searched the Hachette publisher site for an authorized excerpt; the opened title page verified the work but contained no narrative extract.

Searched Google Books, Open Library, and Internet Archive for previews; Google Books exposed metadata/snippets and Open Library listed preview-only editions, neither providing sufficient sustained prose in the opened pages.

Opened the complete text hosted by Adebiet Portal and checked the opening, separated interior locations, the Slote passage, the Bronka/Jastrow scene, and multiple “A Jew’s Journey” headings to distinguish base narration from the embedded manuscript.
person_note: The controlling narration is third-person omniscient: q00013 and the third-person frame in q00021 independently expose an external narrator, while the complete text sustains that position across the opening and interior. The first-person material in q00021 is explicitly labeled as Aaron Jastrow’s manuscript, and the full text repeats that documentary framing, so it is embedded rather than an alternating base narrator. Collective or generic forms such as “us,” “we,” and “one” in historical or gnomic commentary do not make the narrator a participant. No credible contrary source was found; the only potential ambiguity is the recurrence of embedded first-person documents, but their explicit manuscript labels and subordinate placement support THIRD rather than ALTERNATING.
